setlist.title: Sittin' On Top Of The World

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Green, Green Grass Of Home** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer finds this version sweet sounding and regrets that it was dropped from the repertoire; Garcia plays pedal steel on this song [3][4]
- **Old, Old House** (1 review, 1 other source): Rare performance that opens the second set; Only known performance of Old, Old House [1][7]
- **Dire Wolf** (2 reviews): Bob sings Dire Wolf with pedal steel accompaniment, which the reviewer finds especially cool; Bobby sings it, with sweet pedal steel from Jerry [8][14]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Shift from the mellow country-flavored opening songs into this jam signals the band's rapidly expanding approach [6]
- **King Bee** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the King Bee as a standout, energetic performance [7]
- **High Time** (1 other source): Early show has the first known version of High Time, as of January 2003 [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Green, Green Grass Of Home**: rare: 8 archived performances [16]
- **Slewfoot**: rare: 9 archived performances [16]
- **Old, Old House**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- Earliest performances in the archive: High Time, High Time [16]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-21.early-late.aud-sbd.cotsman.16334.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 143 min; rated 2.75/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer wishes a better source existed for the first set, which is currently weak; Best available first-set copy is difficult to listen to; the second set sounds good throughout; First set is nearly unlistenable for sound quality; the second set compensates [4][5][7][12]
- **gd1969-06-21.sbd-late.bove.2195.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 90 min; rated 3.89/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds excellent for a 1969 recording [11]
- **gd1969-06-21.aud-early.cotsman.8995.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 12 songs; 57 min [3]. Said about its sound: High Time cuts out with under a minute likely missing; splices occur in Drums and Cryptical [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer imagines the country material and pedal steel surprised longtime fans in the New York audience [8]
- Garcia plays pedal steel on Green Green Grass, Ol' Slewfoot, Old Old House and Dire Wolf [1]
- Old, Old House also turns up at the Warehouse in New Orleans on Jan 31, 1970 [8]
- Reviewer thinks the first set is the stronger performance, with the second set less good [12]
- Show falls in the era when the band was moving from psychedelia toward country rock [13]
- Reviewer hears the start of the band's move away from psychedelia toward a folksier, western sound [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-21.early-late.aud-sbd.cotsman.16334.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cook and Jeff Cotsman; source: Early: Audience; Late: Soundboard [1]. Also: Matrix combines an audience-recorded first set with a soundboard second set [12]
- **gd1969-06-21.sbd-late.bove.2195.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBDMC(Bear's)=>Dick's C=>DAT=>CDR [2]
- **gd1969-06-21.aud-early.cotsman.8995.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jeff Cook; transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: AUD>MR>C>R>R>R>D>CD>EAC>SHN [3]. Also: Audience recording of the early show, normalized and pitch corrected with Sound Forge [3]
